SocketEncryptionUsage.Notes: All HTTP client traffic from the application uses HTTPS/TLS. This includes: - LLM API calls to Google GenAI, OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Anthropic, and Mistral via langchain-* client libraries - Telemetry export via OpenTelemetry OTLP exporter - Sentry SDK error reporting - Langfuse and LangSmith LLM tracing - Google Cloud Secret Manager API calls - HashiCorp Vault API calls (hvac library) - OTDS authentication ticket validation - MCP (Model Context Protocol) server connections including OAuth token endpoint calls - Migration producer/worker secret retrieval calls when SECRETS_MANAGER=google TLS is provided by the operating system's OpenSSL/LibreSSL through Python's built-in ssl module; the application contains no cipher or protocol selection logic of its own.
SocketEncryptionUsage.Process: FastAPI application process (uvicorn); outbound HTTPS requests via httpx / requests.
Celery worker process; outbound HTTPS requests via requests / google-api-core.

SocketEncryptionUsage.Notes: The FastAPI application is served by uvicorn which supports TLS termination via the --ssl-keyfile / --ssl-certfile options. In standard Kubernetes deployments, TLS termination is done at the ingress layer; uvicorn is not required to handle it directly. Helm chart configuration defines ingress TLS secrets and HSTS annotations for public endpoints. WebSocket endpoint (/v1/chat/stream) are served by FastAPI; when exposed through TLS-enabled ingress they are used as secure WebSocket connections (wss://). Cipher suite selection is delegated entirely to OpenSSL defaults.

SocketEncryptionUsage.Notes: Database connections to PostgreSQL can be established with SSL enabled. The SSL mode is configurable via the POSTGRES_CONNECTION_ARGS setting (e.g., sslmode=require). TLS is provided by the psycopg and psycopg2 libraries which link against OpenSSL.

AuthEncryptionUsage.Notes: OAuth 2.0 (RFC 6749) is used by the MCP (Model Context Protocol) client to authenticate to OAuth-protected MCP servers. Supported grant types: - client_credentials - password (resource owner password credentials) Bearer tokens are transmitted over HTTPS only. The implementation performs no cryptographic operations itself; it submits credentials to a configurable token_url and forwards the returned access token as an HTTP Authorization header.

Implementation.SourceLocation: MCPAuthSchema — client_id / client_secret / token_url configuration model
Implementation.ThirdPartyLocation: HTTP POST to token endpoint over TLS
Implementation.Notes: OAuth is selected as "Other" protocol because the DTD does not list OAuth explicitly. The underlying transport security (TLS) is covered separately in SocketEncryptionUsage entry #1.

DataEncryptionUsage.Data: Document chunk text content is hashed with SHA-256 to produce a deterministic fingerprint used for deduplication when upserting vectors into the pgvector store. Tenant IDs are also hashed to derive short identifier suffixes for PostgreSQL schema names. No data is encrypted for confidentiality purposes; the hash is one-way and non-secret.

Algorithm.name: SHA-256
Algorithm.Notes: Used solely as a one-way hash (data integrity / deduplication), not for encryption or key derivation. Python standard library hashlib.sha256().

Implementation.SourceLocation: compute_chunk_hash() — SHA-256 of normalised chunk text
